newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ford to idle Australian plant for four days.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ford to idle Australian plant for four days.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's Australian unit said on Friday that overstocking would force it to suspend production of cars, utilities and panel vans at its Geelong, Victoria plant for four days over the next two months.
"The days have been planned in response to the current overstocking situation and current slowing in demand levels across the automotive industry as a whole," Ford said in a statement.
The shutdown days are planned for February 11 and 12 and March 11 and 12.

"Ford Motor Co considered it prudent to take this step now to maintain the current rate of production on the lines, rather than take the more disruptive step of slowing the line rates," the company said.
Ford public affairs manager Richard Power said the company's usual daily production was about 440 cars and and between 30 and 35 utilities and panelvans a day.
Power said the company would have to examine prevailing market conditions before deciding on any additional shutdowns during the year.
Ford employees' would still recieve full wages during the shutdowns, the firm said.
Earlier this month, the Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries (FCAI) said Australian new vehicle sales were expected to fall three percent in 1997.
New vehicle sales rose 1.2 percent in calendar 1996 compared with 1995, the FCAI said.
